<p class="theme-lead">Problems rarely come alone. A factory faces many related scheduling scenarios; a logistics company solves new variants of routing every day. Instead of learning each from scratch, my research <b>reuses knowledge</b> — through <b>transfer</b> learning, <b>multitask</b> learning and <b>lifelong</b> learning — so that solvers learn faster and generalise further.</p>

<a name="introduction"></a>
<h2>Introduction</h2>
<h3>Three ways to reuse knowledge</h3>
<p><b>Transfer learning</b> reuses what was learned on a source task to speed up a target task. <b>Multitask learning</b> solves several related tasks together so they help each other. <b>Lifelong learning</b> faces a stream of tasks and must keep improving without forgetting earlier ones.</p>

<a name="contributions"></a>
<h2>My Contributions</h2>
<p>With my students and collaborators, I have made the following contributions. The papers shown are selected automatically: award-winning papers, papers with 100+ citations, and papers in top venues. Click a title to read the paper, or <i>list entry</i> to see it in my publication list.</p>

<h3 class="theme-sub"><span class="theme-sub__num">1</span> Knowledge transfer in genetic programming</h3>
<p>We transfer useful sub-trees, individuals and search distributions between GP runs on related routing problems, and studied how reusable evolved rules are.</p>
<ul class="contrib-list">
  <li><a class="contrib-list__title" href="https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-030-72069-8_9">Knowledge Transfer in Genetic Programming Hyper-heuristics</a><span class="contrib-list__venue"><i>Automated Design of Machine Learning and Search Algorithms</i>, 2021 · <a href="/publications/publication-chapter.html#mei2021knowledge">list entry</a></span> <span class="contrib-list__note">Book chapter</span></li>

<h3 class="theme-sub"><span class="theme-sub__num">3</span> Lifelong learning for optimisation</h3>
<p>When new problem variants keep arriving, a learner must adapt without forgetting. We consolidate past behaviour to keep performance on earlier tasks while learning new ones.</p>
